rationale: design-import-refactor: generic change landed in Pulp per owner decision 2026-10-04; Vellum inherits (see inheritance ledger); RuntimeEffectCache no longer refuses caller SkSL that declares a local named pos in main(). The refusal existed only because Skia before chrome/m158 let that local redefine or shadow the coordinate parameter Graphite names pos; on the chrome/m158 Skia this branch pins, Graphite renders such shaders identically to a control, so the refusal rejected valid shaders on every backend. pulp-test-runtime-effect-names-gpu now requires every name-alike shader, including a local pos in main and a nested pos shadowing the coordinates, to compile and match the control ramp on live Graphite, so a Skia that reintroduces the collision fails there. No public API is removed and no design-import, rendering, packaging, or source-authority boundary moves.
tests: ctest --test-dir build -R 'Runtime-effect locals named like Graphite'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'compile_sksl accepts locals named pos in main'
